480	The Chida, of blessed memory, in his book Pnei David, writes that the angels had
481	a claim against Moshe Rabbenu.
482	Why?
483	They said, this rabbi is not of proper lineage.
484	HaShem said to them, what do you mean he is not of proper lineage?
485	This is Moshe Rabbenu, son of Amram: "A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi." How can you say he is not of proper lineage?
486	They said, excuse us, who is his mother?
487	He said to them, what, who is his mother?
488	Yocheved, she was a righteous woman, what do you mean who is his mother?
489	They said, true, but Amram divorced his wife Yocheved.
490	And Yocheved went and married Elitzafan, and bore from him
491	Eldad and Medad.
492	Therefore Eldad and Medad are brothers of Moshe from the same mother but not the same father.
493	That is Eldad and Medad, and so the Ramban also writes.
494	Afterward Elitzafan and Yocheved decided they were not suited to each other.
495	She divorced him
496	and returned to Amram.
497	So it turns out that Moshe Rabbenu is a son, when she returned to Amram, then she bore Moshe
498	Rabbenu.
499	So Moshe Rabbenu is the son of a man who took back his divorced wife after her remarriage, which is forbidden.
500	Did you understand the move that happened here?
501	In the Torah it is forbidden to do such a thing.
502	Why is it forbidden?
503	If a man divorced his wife, and she went and married someone else, and now she has divorced
504	him, and she wants to go back to the first one, her first husband, she cannot do that according to the Torah.
505	Why?
506	So that people will not swap wives.
507	How does that work?
508	Say, I am here, say there are two men, me and my wife, and another
509	man and his wife.
510	Now, heaven forbid, I set my eye on his wife, and he, heaven forbid, set his eye on my wife.
511	What do we do so that everything will be smooth, kosher, by the Torah, mehadrin?
512	I divorce her, he divorces her.
513	I marry his wife, he marries my wife.
514	We do whatever we want, then I divorce her, he divorces her.
515	I take back my wife and he takes back his wife.
516	And everything was perfectly by the book, there is no prohibition here.
517	So you see, the Torah was already wise, and said there is no such thing.
518	One who takes back his divorced wife after her remarriage, if she already married, he can no longer take her back, so that there will be no
519	swapping of wives.
520	Did you understand this trick?
521	And so with Moshe Rabbenu, the angels had a claim about his lineage.
522	What did the angels say?
523	They said, excuse us, he is the son of one who took back his divorced wife after her remarriage.
524	Yocheved was married to Amram.
525	Amram divorced her, and why did he divorce her?
526	He said, what?
527	"Every son that is born, throw into the Nile": I do not want to bring more children.
528	So he did not bring more children.
529	And then he divorced her.
530	She went, did not want to be alone, and married Elitzafan.
531	She bore Eldad and Medad, Elitzafan divorced her, she went and returned to Amram.
532	So now, when Amram took her back, she conceived Moshe.
533	So apparently the angels had a claim against Moshe, that he is the son of one who took back his divorced wife, that the child has a flaw.
534	About this the angels said, "What is one born of woman doing among us?"
535	What does "one born of woman" mean?
536	A woman known to have been taken back after remarriage.
537	What is she doing?
538	HaShem said to them, he came to receive the Torah.
539	What does it mean, to receive the Torah?
540	Now these laws exist, before that these laws did not exist.
541	So everything is fine with him.
542	Now the real question is, why did HaShem bring the soul of Moshe in such a complicated and cumbersome way?
543	Because apparently, setting aside now whether the Torah had been received or not,
544	the main idea here is that the soul of Moshe Rabbenu descended in a chain.
545	As if there was a flaw in the descent of the soul, that of one who takes back his divorced wife after her remarriage.
546	So how can that be?
547	So the Arizal writes, Rabenu HaAri writes, a kind
548	of wonderful teaching, and he brings it in Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 15.
549	He does not speak there about Moshe, but he speaks about the matter of souls of holy people who come within the souls of
550	secular families.
551	You can see this to this day.
552	I think this generation, this Shaar HaGilgulim is the most connected to this generation.
553	If you see a secular family that does not keep Torah and does not keep mitzvot, and the more they are a husk
554	and the more they hate the Torah and Moshe His servant, and hate and are anti and so on,
555	and one of them returned to teshuvah, and it is known that he does not belong to this family at all.
556	What does it mean, does not belong?
557	He does not belong to them.
558	True, they brought him into the world physically, true, bodily he belongs to them.
559	Physiologically, these are their genes.
560	But in the end, in his soul he belongs to especially high souls, whom HaShem did not want to bring through
561	families of distinguished Haredim.
562	Because if He brought them through families of distinguished Haredim, the Sitra Achra would accuse them.
563	And they would not succeed in their studies, would not succeed in holiness, would not succeed in anything, they would fall.
564	From too much...
565	from too much of their holiness.
566	So all day the Sitra Achra, as the Gemara says,
567	page 52, tractate Sukkah: the evil inclination leaves the whole world and goes after Israel.
568	It leaves all of Israel, goes after the Torah scholars.
569	It leaves the Torah scholars, goes after the rabbis.
570	The holier you are, the more the evil inclination comes to make you fall.
571	So what does HaShem do so that the Sitra Achra will not provoke those souls?
572	He brings them through the husk.
573	And so this person has to deal with a bad family, a bad mother, a wicked father, with people
574	who do not keep Torah, with people who desecrate the festivals.
575	And the Ari writes, open it up, it is beautiful, it is also not hard to understand, Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 15.
576	And he writes there, that if we see with our eyes that he grows up and learns a lot of Torah,
577	and becomes a great tzaddik, it is known that what I said is true.
578	And it is known that this is so, that he is a high soul who does not belong at all to this family.
579	So this is a great thing, and this is the reason why HaShem brought Moshe Rabbenu in such a way.
580	Why did He send his soul down in such a way?
581	So that in the end there would be no accusation against his soul.
582	Who has a greater soul than Moshe Rabbenu?
583	Is there anyone?
584	He is equal to 600,000 of Israel.
585	So in order to bring his soul down in the proper way, the soul of Moshe had to be brought through
586	one who takes back his divorced wife after remarriage.
587	This is the reason why HaShem brought the soul of Moshe Rabbenu this way.
588	I said this, I do not remember if I said it here, that I think our righteous Mashiach will be a baal teshuvah.
589	Once I said this in Moussaïoff, right when I came to give classes there, seven and a half
590	years ago.
591	I gave a class there, and I said that our righteous Mashiach will be a baal teshuvah.
592	And it angered all the Haredim there, how dare I.
593	Our righteous Mashiach will be a baal teshuvah, and all the Haredim turn up their noses at you, as if you are, they look down on you.
594	This is one more of the...
595	of the great disappointments of the baal teshuvah.
596	He enters the world of Torah and thinks everything is beautiful, and at least you will get feedback
597	from the religious, and you see worse than what you see outside.
598	You understand that you need to create your own kingdom, you need to create a bubble, an environment
599	of your own, for you, for your children, and not to mix in too much.
